short_title: Why you should never wash raw chicken 🐔 #shorts
short_description:
Rinsing raw chicken doesn't wash germs away: the splashing spreads them. Water droplets can travel about two feet around the sink (UK Food Standards Agency). In a 2019 USDA kitchen study, 60% of people who rinsed raw poultry had bacteria in their sink afterward. Vinegar or lemon won't make it safe: only cooking to 165°F (74°C) inside the meat kills the bacteria (USDA, CDC). And wash your hands for 20 seconds after touching raw chicken.

Do you wash yours? Send this to someone who still washes chicken 👇

More everyday habits: https://youtube.com/shorts/D2dTGiROFtg

Sources: USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service (2019 observational study), CDC, UK Food Standards Agency.
